```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
has_quanteda <- requireNamespace("quanteda", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("quanteda") >= "4.5.0"
```

A word can occur near a node often simply because it is common. To describe
association, compare the observed number of pairs with an expected number
computed from an explicit population of possible pairs. Keep both counts:
a high association score from one occurrence deserves different interpretation
from a frequently repeated combination.

This guide uses ldfreq 0.3.0.9010 or later and optional **quanteda >= 4.5.0**.
It starts with adjacent words, then expands to a left/right span. The two
helpers in `examples/collocation.R` use the saved searches from
`examples/concordance.R`. These are explicitly sourced, installed examples,
not exported functions. The examples below are authored for hand checking;
they are not learner data or an assessment of annotation accuracy.

## Start with a complete, source-linked search

```{r collocation-demo, eval=has_quanteda}
library(ldfreq)

demo <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("examples", "collocation-demo.R",
  package = "ldfreq", mustWork = TRUE), demo)
helper <- demo$helper
search <- demo$search
print(demo$annotations$segments, row.names = FALSE)
```

The imported tokens retain original positions and character offsets. The
chosen `lemma` column is missing for `gap`; the comma is explicitly excluded.
`d2` has two separate segments. Every segment is a hard boundary. A segment
means a sentence only when your input defines it as one; the helper does not
split sentences automatically.

For your own unchanged `lexdiv_import_annotations()` result, source both
helpers and make a search. See the [concordance guide](concordance-and-dispersion.html)
for preparing aligned annotations from your text or parser output.

```{r own-collocation, eval=FALSE}
helper <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
for (file in c("concordance.R", "collocation.R"))
  sys.source(system.file("examples", file, package = "ldfreq", mustWork = TRUE), helper)
search <- helper$concordance_search(annotations, list(node = "learn"),
  term_col = "lemma", keep = keep, window = 5L)
nearby <- helper$collocation_profile(search, "node", span = c(left = 3L, right = 3L))
```

A node query must have one token pattern. Fixed, wildcard and regular-expression
queries retain their saved search settings. A pattern matching several forms
pools those node positions into one class. Context terms use exact UTF-8 values
of the selected column: the node's case-insensitive matching does **not** merge
context forms such as `Word` and `word`. No new case or Unicode normalization
is performed. Specify and preserve any normalization in the annotations.

## Adjacent words: inspect the denominator first

```{r adjacent, eval=has_quanteda}
adjacent <- helper$collocation_profile(search, "a") # L0/R1
print(adjacent$results, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
print(adjacent$documents, row.names = FALSE)
```

There are **8 eligible adjacent pairs**, of which **3** start at the node `a`.
The context `b` appears at the right endpoint of **3** eligible pairs, and the
pair `a b` occurs **2** times. Thus its expected count is
`3 * 3 / 8 = 1.125`. These marginals count positions in eligible pairs,
not unrestricted unigram frequencies. Final tokens, excluded endpoints and
segment boundaries affect the denominator.

For each context type, the result includes:

| Column | Meaning in the saved pair population |
|---|---|
| `observed` | Pairs with both a matching node and this context term, O |
| `node_marginal` | All pairs whose node endpoint matches the query, R |
| `context_marginal` | All pairs whose context endpoint has this term, C |
| `opportunities` | All eligible ordered pairs, N |
| `expected` | R × C / N, E |
| `MI` | Pointwise mutual information, log2(O / E) |
| `t_score` | (O − E) / sqrt(O) |
| `documents` | Distinct documents contributing to O |
| `context_documents` | Distinct documents contributing to C |
| `meets_min_count` | Display-selection flag; counts remain complete |
| `status` | `ok`, `zero_observed`, or `no_node_opportunities` |

The MI and t-score definitions follow Evert's
[association-measure discussion](https://www.stephanie-evert.de/PUB/Evert2007HSK_extended_manuscript.pdf),
Sections 4.1–4.3. MI is sensitive to rare combinations; report O and choose a
frequency threshold explicitly. Here t-score is a descriptive association
measure, not a Student t statistic or a significance test. Overlapping windows
share tokens, and documents may share writers; these rows are not independent
observations for a study-level model.

The helper applies **no smoothing**. When O = 0 and E > 0, MI is `-Inf` and
t-score is `NA` (`zero_observed`). When no eligible pair starts at a matching
node, E = 0 and both scores are `NA` (`no_node_opportunities`). With no eligible
pairs at all, the results table is empty and document status explains why.
Only context types present in eligible pairs receive rows. An absent row is
not a claim of zero frequency in an external corpus, and a missing lemma is
not a known zero.

## Expand the span without changing the meaning of a position

```{r span, eval=has_quanteda}
span <- helper$collocation_profile(search, "a", span = c(left = 2L, right = 2L))
print(span$results, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
print(span$documents[c("document_id", "candidate_slot_pairs",
  "eligible_pairs", "excluded_pairs", "node_occurrences", "nodes_with_context", "node_pairs")],
  row.names = FALSE)
```

The span example has **30 eligible ordered pairs**. Each ordered pair of
original positions within the requested distance is one opportunity. Both
endpoints must be searchable, and they must belong to the same segment.
The span includes all distances from 1 to the chosen width on each side;
`left = 0` or `right = 0` selects only the other direction.

These rules determine the counts:

- A node token cannot pair with itself. Two occurrences of the same word can
  pair with each other. With both directions enabled, `(i, j)` and `(j, i)`
  are separate ordered opportunities.
- Repeated context tokens each count. Two node tokens may pair with the same
  context token: their original position pairs are different.
- Excluded or missing endpoints cannot form a pair. Intervening excluded or
  missing slots still consume distance and do not block a wider-span pair.
  Thus `a , b` can contribute at distance +2, but never at +1. Splitting the
  input into sentence segments is the way to prohibit sentence crossing.
- Node and context marginals and N are recounted over this whole pair
  population. Do not substitute corpus unigram totals, or multiply the node
  frequency by twice the span: boundaries and endpoint availability matter.
- Left and right distances are pooled within a call. To describe one side,
  run a separate call with the other width zero; filtering the saved pairs
  afterward would invalidate the original scores and denominators.

This is an independence model for the two roles in a population of **ordered
token pairs**. It is not the conventional surface-window approximation using
unigram frequencies times span width. Scores from tools using different
populations or exclusion rules need not agree.

The complete `$pairs` table contains background opportunities as well as
matching node pairs. `$documents` retains empty and zero-match documents,
original/searchable/missing token counts, candidate and eligible pair counts,
node occurrences, and nodes with at least one eligible context.
By default, `max_pairs = 1e6` bounds **all candidate slot pairs before endpoint
exclusions**. Exceeding the bound raises an error rather than truncating the
sample. This is not a full memory bound or a streaming large-corpus engine.

## Select frequent combinations and return to their source

```{r select-context, eval=has_quanteda}
selected <- helper$collocation_profile(search, "a", min_count = 2L)
shown <- subset(selected$results, meets_min_count)
shown <- shown[order(-shown$MI, -shown$observed), ]
print(shown, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

`min_count` is a positive whole number. It sets a flag; it never removes pairs,
changes marginals, or overwrites below-threshold counts. The default of 1
includes singletons for inspection and is not a recommendation for ranking
rare combinations. Choose a threshold appropriate to your corpus and report it.

```{r source-context, eval=has_quanteda}
pairs <- subset(span$pairs, is_node & context_term == "b")
kwic <- span$search$occurrences[
  match(pairs$occurrence_id, span$search$occurrences$occurrence_id), ]
inspection <- data.frame(document_id = pairs$document_id,
  segment_id = pairs$segment_id, node_position = pairs$node_position,
  context_position = pairs$context_position, distance = pairs$distance,
  pre = kwic$pre, node = kwic$keyword, post = kwic$post,
  context = span$search$source$tokens$surface[pairs$context_row])
print(inspection, row.names = FALSE)
```

Each matching pair links to a saved node occurrence ID, original token rows and
segment-local, 1-based inclusive character offsets. A node KWIC may appear
more than once because it contributed several pairs. Its display window comes
from the original search; choose a search window at least as wide as the
collocation span to see all the context in this display. The full original
segment remains available even with a narrower KWIC window.

## Save the complete record and replay it

```{r save-collocation, eval=has_quanteda}
record <- list(adjacent = adjacent, span = span, session = sessionInfo())
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") # use a durable project path for your analysis
saveRDS(record, file, version = 2)
reopened <- readRDS(file)
helper$collocation_validate(reopened$span)
replayed <- helper$collocation_profile(reopened$span$search, "a",
  span = reopened$span$settings$span)
stopifnot(identical(replayed, reopened$span))
unlink(file)
```

Retain the full object, source annotations, helper/package versions and session
information; a CSV of selected scores cannot reconstruct the denominator.
`collocation_validate()` detects accidental changes to the saved record, including
its search. It is not an authenticity check for supplied annotations. Exact
whole-object replay requires the same package version; after an upgrade, compare
counts and settings explicitly instead of assuming object identity.

## What was checked, and what the scores do not establish

The authored example's adjacent pairs agree with `lexdiv_ngrams()`. A separate
Cartesian enumeration verifies the pair sets and 2×2 tables for left-only,
right-only and two-sided spans, including segment boundaries, repeated nodes,
excluded endpoints and missing terms. Positive-count scores were checked against
`corpora` 0.7's [am.score()](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/corpora/corpora.pdf)
with the same positional marginals and `span.size = 1`: the span is already
represented by the pair population. The deliberate `NA` t-score convention at
O = 0 is checked separately. `corpora` is not needed to run these helpers.

These checks concern counting and numerical reproduction on constructed data.
They do not validate idiomaticity, semantic cohesion, language proficiency,
or performance on a natural corpus. Phrase nodes, dependency relations and
automatic sentence detection are outside this example. The existing
[n-gram reference profiles](ngram-profiles.html) retain their own frequency and
coverage contracts; a pruned reference table cannot supply missing marginals.
Preserve writer, task and occasion identifiers when relating text measures
to research outcomes, as in the [repeated-observations guide](repeated-observations.html).
